title: What Is NPS? Net Promoter Score: Definition and Tips - Shopify

facts.fact: The standard NPS survey question asks customers to rate on a scale of 0 to 10 how likely they are to recommend the company to a friend.
facts.quote: On a scale of 0 to 10, how likely are you to recommend us to a friend?

facts.fact: NPS respondents answering 9 or 10 are classified as promoters.
facts.quote: answer with a 9 or 10. They are enthusiastic advocates for your company.

facts.fact: NPS respondents answering 7 or 8 are classified as passives.
facts.quote: answer with a 7 or 8. They are mildly enthusiastic about your business.

facts.fact: NPS respondents answering 6 or below are classified as detractors.
facts.quote: respond with a score of 6 or below.

facts.fact: The page gives the NPS formula as the percentage of promoters minus the percentage of detractors, multiplied by 100.
facts.value: NPS = [(number of promoters / total number of respondents) - (number of detractors / total number of respondents)] x 100
facts.quote: NPS = [(number of promoters / total number of respondents) - (number of detractors / total number of respondents)] x 100

facts.fact: In the page's worked example, a survey of 100 people with 40 promoters, 50 passives, and 10 detractors yields an NPS of 30.
facts.quote: If your company surveys 100 people and has 40 promoters, 50 passives, and 10 detractors, your NPS calculation will read:

facts.fact: The page's own example calculation shows NPS = (40/100 - 10/100) x 100 = 30.
The page states that scores vary considerably by industry, so many companies consult industry benchmarks to set targets, but it gives no numeric benchmark.
facts.quote: Because scores vary considerably by industry, however, many companies consult industry benchmarks to determine individual targets.
